title: Remodeling: Maps-first discovery with permit activity safeguards
hypothesis: A public contractor register or recent general-contractor permit can corroborate remodeling activity, but a permit contractor, qualifier, and published business phone remain candidates until remodel relevance, independent ownership evidence, line-type, live, DNC, and dedupe gates pass.
ownerSource: Maps-first remodeling discovery plus a legally usable contractor register or Austin permit contractor field as candidate-only identity/activity evidence. No current source in this route independently proves the permit contact owns the business.
phoneSource: Published Maps or Austin contractor phone as one business-contact candidate. It is not an owner-confirmed mobile merely because a city permit publishes it.

workflow.label: Discover remodeling candidate
workflow.detail: Start from the live recipe-A kitchen-remodeling query or a lawful register/permit candidate.

workflow.label: Remodeling relevance
workflow.detail: Require remodel, renovation, kitchen/bath remodel, or design-build evidence; generic contractors and trade-only specialists need review.

workflow.label: Hold off-target contractor
workflow.detail: Do not classify general, mechanical, electrical, cabinet, flooring, tile, franchise, or commercial-only rows as remodelers without positive evidence.

workflow.label: Optional permit or register corroboration
workflow.detail: Use current activity and named contractor role only after legal and remodeling-fit checks; a permit contact is a candidate, not owner proof.

workflow.label: Candidate role supported?
workflow.detail: Retain a sole owner or independently supported principal separately; keep Permit Contractor, filer, qualifier, and employee roles as candidates.

workflow.label: Hold unsupported owner claim
workflow.detail: Keep the business lead without an owner label when role evidence is absent or ambiguous.

workflow.label: Published business contact
workflow.detail: Use a Maps or permit phone once only when it is published and not already shared or suppressed.

workflow.label: Hold missing or shared contact
workflow.detail: Do not infer a private phone or treat a repeated office number as a direct owner contact.

workflow.label: Contact and compliance gates
workflow.detail: Apply mobile line-type, live, DNC, global dedupe, and required ownership-evidence checks.

workflow.label: Hold failed verification
workflow.detail: Park non-mobile, unreachable, DNC, duplicate, or unsupported-owner cases.

workflow.label: Deliver supported classification
workflow.detail: Deliver only after every required gate passes; owner-confirmed mobile requires independent ownership evidence.

edges.label: all contact and owner-evidence gates pass

failures.risk: The broad remodeling allow pattern admits a generic contractor or permit trade as a remodeler.
failures.mitigation: Require positive remodel, renovation, kitchen/bath remodel, or design-build evidence before retaining an Austin or register candidate.

failures.risk: A kitchen, bath, cabinet, flooring, or tile specialist is represented as a full-service remodeler.
failures.mitigation: Treat adjacent specialties as review/hold unless an explicit remodel signal is also present.

failures.risk: A permit contractor, filer, qualifier, or employee is represented as business owner.
failures.mitigation: Persist Permit Contractor as candidate role and require independent ownership evidence before owner labeling.

failures.risk: Austin contractor_phone is called a direct owner mobile.
failures.mitigation: Treat it as a published business contact and require exclusivity, line type, live, DNC, dedupe, and independent ownership evidence.

failures.risk: A stale Austin schema-failure claim blocks a currently available source, or future schema drift goes unnoticed.
failures.mitigation: Use a required-field schema guard and freeze the adapter only if contractor fields are actually absent.

iterations.hypothesis: The Austin permit route was unavailable because its contractor fields had been removed from the current schema.
iterations.test: Free aggregate-only live metadata and endpoint audit on 2026-09-24: inspect field names, request the adapter's seven-field select without retaining values, and count contractor-field presence for rows issued after 2025-09-24.
iterations.observed: Metadata listed 78 columns including contractor_trade, contractor_company_name, contractor_full_name, contractor_phone, and applicant fields; the configured select returned HTTP 200. Among 55,154 recent permits, contractor_trade was present on 51,761, contractor_company_name on 50,077, contractor_full_name on 50,904, and contractor_phone on 51,118. These are all-trade coverage counts, not remodeling or owner outcomes.
iterations.change: Unblock the source only as an optional general-contractor activity/candidate route, require remodeling relevance before use, and add a required-field schema guard rather than relying on stale failure evidence.

measurement.result: Current Austin endpoint schema audit: a five-row issue_date-only response succeeded; metadata and aggregate-only field counts verified contractor fields. For 55,154 rows issued after 2025-09-24, contractor_trade 51,761, contractor_company_name 50,077, contractor_full_name 50,904, contractor_phone 51,118. No identities, addresses, or phone values were retained. The observation does not measure remodeling fit, mobile status, reachability, DNC, owner confirmation, or delivery.

cost.basis: Free public-schema and aggregate field-coverage observation only
cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. Historical remodeling brain rates have a different denominator and are unchanged.

implementation.summary: Remodeling is recipe A and has a relevance profile. Austin's adapter is live and its selected fields currently exist, but remodeling has no register mapping and register ingestion does not apply remodeling relevance to Austin contractor_trade. Enabling the source without a filter would admit general, mechanical, or electrical permit rows.

nextMeasurement: Add synthetic Austin rows for remodeling-positive, generic general-contractor, and mechanical/electrical cases; prove only the remodel-positive row can enter a remodeling candidate path and that Permit Contractor plus phone cannot create an owner label. After authorization, measure remodel fit, mobile type, DNC, reachability, owner confirmation, and delivery with separate denominators.
